title: Slow 60-day breakout with 200-day regime filter and 30-day trend exit
ex_ante_rule: Use closed 1h candles only; signals evaluated at bar close, order executed at next bar open. Long only, one position, whole balance. ENTRY: close > highest high of the prior 1440 bars (60 days, excluding current bar) AND close > SMA(4800 bars, 200 days) of close AND no open position. EXIT: close < lowest low of the prior 720 bars (30 days, excluding current bar), OR close below entry price by 15% (hard stop, checked on closed bars). After any exit, no re-entry until at least 168 bars (7 days) have passed. No other filters, no pyramiding, no take-profit.
rationale: Time-series momentum in crypto: price at new multi-month highs inside a long-term uptrend tends to keep drifting because of slow-moving capital inflow, under-reaction to information and trend-chasing by retail, so a trend follower is paid for bearing drawdown risk and for the hedgers/contrarians who sell too early. The prior Donchian 20/10 variant traded about 800 times per pair and was killed by costs and whipsaws; here lookbacks are 60/30 days plus a 7-day cooldown, so I expect roughly 3-8 trades per year per pair. Winning trades in trends historically move +20% to +100%, far above the 0.35-0.5% round-trip cost, while losers are capped near -15% and the 30-day low exit usually cuts them sooner. Edge is not guaranteed; the mechanism is documented in crypto TSMOM literature, but I found no source for these exact lengths, which are round numbers chosen a priori.
novelty_vs_tried: Differs from H-002 (Donchian 20/10, ~800 trades) by using 3x/3x longer channels, a 200-day regime filter, and a cooldown, cutting trade count by ~100x so cost drag is minor. Differs from H-001 (SMA crossover) and H-003 (short-horizon mean reversion, opposite premise) by using a slow new-high breakout with a long-low trailing exit rather than crossover or oversold bounce.
